pages.expectedH1: What Is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?
pages.title: What Is MCP (Model Context Protocol)? - Model Context Protocol Hub | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: Learn what the Model Context Protocol (MCP) is, how client-server connections work, and explore our comprehensive directory of supported integrations and related topics.
pages.h1: What Is MCP (Model Context Protocol)?

pages.expectedH1: MCP Server
pages.title: MCP Server - Model Context Protocol Hub | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: An MCP server is a program that exposes tools, resources, or reusable prompts to an AI application through the Model Context Protocol. A host application creates an MCP client connection to the server, negotiates capabilities, and invokes supported functions through JSON-RPC.
pages.h1: MCP Server

pages.expectedH1: MCP Architecture
pages.title: MCP Architecture - Model Context Protocol Hub | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: MCP architecture separates the user-facing host, the protocol client inside that host, and one or more MCP servers that expose tools, resources, and prompts. The client and server exchange JSON-RPC messages over stdio for local processes or Streamable HTTP for remote deployments.
pages.h1: MCP Architecture

pages.expectedH1: MCP Client
pages.title: MCP Client - Model Context Protocol Hub | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: An MCP client is any application that can connect to MCP servers, discover tools, and invoke them – e.g., Claude Desktop, Cursor, or a custom app.
pages.h1: MCP Client

pages.expectedH1: MCP Host
pages.title: MCP Host - Model Context Protocol Hub | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: An MCP host is the application the user interacts with, such as an AI desktop app, IDE, or agent runtime. The host creates MCP client connections, applies user and workspace policy, and decides how tool, resource, and prompt results appear in the model workflow.
pages.h1: MCP Host

pages.expectedH1: MCP Tools
pages.title: MCP Tools - Model Context Protocol Hub | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: MCP tools are executable functions exposed by an MCP server, allowing AI agents to perform actions like file access, database queries, and API calls.
pages.h1: MCP Tools

pages.expectedH1: MCP Resources
pages.title: MCP Resources - Model Context Protocol Hub | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: MCP resources are data objects that a server makes available for clients to read, such as files, database records, schemas, or generated context. They complement tools: resources provide context, while tools perform actions or compute results.
pages.h1: MCP Resources

pages.expectedH1: MCP Prompts
pages.title: MCP Prompts - Model Context Protocol Hub | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: MCP prompts are reusable, parameterized prompt templates that a server can expose to a host. They help teams standardize workflows such as code review, database analysis, incident triage, or support responses without hard-coding instructions into every client.
pages.h1: MCP Prompts

pages.expectedH1: Discover. Deploy. Scale. Everything MCP.
pages.title: MCP Server Directory - Explore 100+ Integrations - MCPserver.in | MCPserver.in
pages.metaDescription: Browse the curated directory of Model Context Protocol (MCP) servers. Integrate databases, web APIs, developer tools, and SaaS platforms side-by-side.
pages.h1: Discover. Deploy. Scale. Everything MCP.
